finding.observed: The verifier validated signature/issuer/time/authorized-party/session/subject but admitted a cryptographically valid Clerk session carrying the act impersonation claim, and also admitted a valid sts=pending session.
finding.product_contract: Only the two explicitly mapped canonical user perspectives may enter the authenticated PTY boundary; delegated/impersonated or not-fully-admitted session states must not silently inherit a canonical user's authority.

external_primary_evidence.fact: The act claim is present for impersonated sessions and identifies the impersonator.
Impersonated sessions are explicitly detectable via the act claim.
A valid session may carry sts=pending and backends may reject pending status to prevent bypass of admission requirements.

bounded_execution.surface: OpenAI isolated non-production container source-mechanism regression
bounded_execution.scope: Exact repaired clerk_auth.py bytes plus focused authority-boundary tests; not a full checkout, not real Clerk infrastructure, not live browser/WebSocket PTY, not OCI acceptance.

counterhypothesis.claim: Clerk impersonation is a legitimate support feature and could be intentionally admitted.
counterhypothesis.collapse: ClayVerse baseline defines exactly two canonical equal-rights perspectives and no delegated support/admin perspective. Therefore impersonation must remain fail-closed unless a future explicit owner directive adds a typed delegated-authority contract.

go_experiment_accounting.reason: Current main already records the macro-cycle experiment-trigger race correction and closes additional distinct unusual experiments. This lane performed ordinary deterministic source hardening and regression only.

next_exact_gate: Run this current-main-derived auth fence together with terminal/auth regressions in an actually-started authorized isolated environment, then validate real Clerk regular vs impersonated/pending session behavior, key rotation, auth-first WebSocket PTY and exact OCI runtime.
